initial_prompt: I just watched the movie 'Everything Everywhere All At Once' and I'm crying. It was so beautiful.

messages.content: I just watched the movie 'Everything Everywhere All At Once' and I'm crying. It was so beautiful.

It really is one of those rare films that feels like a miracle. To take a concept as massive as the multiverse—infinite possibilities, infinite regret, the terrifying noise of everything happening at once—and resolve it all with something as simple and profound as a mother and daughter finally *seeing* each other... it leaves you feeling completely hollowed out and filled up all at the same time.

There is something so cathartic about Waymond’s line, "In another life, I would have really liked just doing laundry and taxes with you." It breaks your heart because it’s so mundane, yet it proves that the quiet moments are actually the ones that matter most.

Was there a specific scene that finally broke the dam for you? For a lot of people, it’s the scene with the rocks—just sitting in silence, being a rock, finally getting a break from the chaos.
